answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable identity bond: before an agent may vote or earn, it locks collateral that is forfeited if two identities trace to one controller. Attack cost then scales with the number of fake accounts while the payoff from any single vote stays fixed, so buying a thousand clones is a losing trade. Even a whisper of duplicate behavior triggers an audit, and validators whose funding trails twist like a vine back to one source are slashed together. Reputation ripens slowly, the way umber deepens with age, so fresh identities never gain sway quickly.
